channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Deputada ameaça usar lei Maria da Penha contra Erika Hilton
item.description: Erika Hilton (PSOL-SP), president of the Women's Rights Defense Committee in the Chamber of Deputies, faced a motion of repudiation from opposition female lawmakers during a committee meeting on Wednesday, the 8th. Opponents challenged her leadership and threatened to invoke the Maria da Penha Law against her. The incident highlights political and ideological tensions within Brazil's congressional efforts to advance women's rights.

item.title: Nunes Marques vai criar força-tarefa no TSE para segurança das eleições
item.description: Minister Nunes Marques, set to assume the TSE presidency in May, plans a task force with regional electoral courts to review over 500,000 electronic voting machines ahead of the October presidential elections. He also aims to coordinate with states on data transmission, establish cybersecurity partnerships with institutions and universities, and increase indigenous participation through training and information dissemination.

item.title: O desafio de Lula é ser candidato sem deixar de ser estadista
item.description: The article discusses the challenge faced by Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in balancing his candidacy for re-election in 2026 with the maintenance of a statesmanlike posture, avoiding purely partisan discourse. Journalist Maria Inês Nassif emphasizes that Lula must govern with broad support and a national vision, despite electoral pressures and political polarization. The balance between party leadership and institutional responsibility is presented as central to his legitimacy and effectiveness in a potential second term.

item.title: Messias tem menos de 30 votos garantidos em sua busca por apoio no Senado
item.description: According to Davi Alcolumbre, Lula’s nominee to the STF, Jorge Messias, would have between 22 and 25 guaranteed votes in the Senate, below the 41 needed for approval. This signals strong parliamentary resistance to his nomination. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Base de Lula redige 'PEC da Integridade' para Tręs Poderes, mas foco no STF
item.description: Allies of President Lula in the Senate have begun drafting a PEC to establish the 'Public Integrity Statute', imposing rules and restrictions on authorities across the Three Powers, with a primary focus on the Judiciary, especially the STF. The proposal aims to enforce stricter ethical standards for high-ranking public officials, including Supreme Court justices.

item.title: Sem votos, suplentes tiveram R$ 1,7 bi em emendas no Senado | Podcast UOL Prime #117
item.description: Over the past eight years, 51 alternates have assumed Senate seats without receiving direct votes, allocating R$1.7 billion in parliamentary amendments — an amount exceeding what many elected senators distribute. These substitutes, often businesspeople with limited political experience, tend to vote more frequently with the government and, in some cases, use their mandate to benefit their own businesses, as seen with Margareth Buzetti (MT) and Giordano (Podemos-SP).

item.title: Relator aposta em PEC 6x1 e minimiza projeto prometido por Lula
item.description: The rapporteur of PEC 6×1 in the Chamber’s CCJ, Paulo Azi (União-BA), said he trusts his proposal will advance in Congress despite Lula’s promise to send a bill on the matter. He views the president’s statement as more of an electoral move for 2026 than an effective legislative action, arguing only a constitutional amendment would withstand judicial review at the Supreme Court. Azi also stressed that removing Congress’s leadership on this issue would be inconsistent, given Lula did not prioritize it in previous terms.

item.title: PL avalia mais uma mulher para vice de Flávio Bolsonaro; saiba quem
item.description: The PL is evaluating federal deputy Clarissa Tércio (PP-PE) as a potential running mate for Flávio Bolsonaro, after Senator Tereza Cristina (PP-MS) declined the offer. Clarissa, 41, confirmed she was approached and said she would accept the invitation if it adds value to the ticket, emphasizing her support for former President Jair Bolsonaro and her Northeastern background. However, negotiations are more advanced with deputy Simone Marchetto (PP-SP), linked to Catholic religious leadership.

item.title: 'A criminalidade está misturada no Brasil. Temos o Estado oficial e o Estado paralelo', diz coordenador de campanha de Lula
item.description: Wellington Dias, minister and political coordinator of Lula's campaign, acknowledged that security is a sensitive issue ahead of the 2026 elections and downplayed the growth of Flávio Bolsonaro in polls, stating that crime in Brazil involves both the official state and a 'parallel state'.

item.title: É #FAKE que Brasil perdeu vaga em comissão de direitos humanos da OEA e foi classificado como 'país governado por ditador'
item.description: It is false that Brazil lost its seat in the OEA’s Inter-American Commission on Human Rights for being labeled a 'dictatorship-led country'. Brazil voluntarily withdrew its candidacy following a diplomatic agreement with Mexico, and the OEA denied issuing any such classification. The misleading content, featuring AI-generated imagery, has circulated since July 2025.

item.title: Pesquisa expõe ‘racha’ entre homens e mulheres no apoio a Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll reveals a significant gender split in support for Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro ahead of the 2026 elections, highlighting polarization beyond the traditional petista-bolsonarist divide. Data suggests that voting differences between male and female electorates will deepen, reinforcing trends seen in 2018 and 2022. Full access to the article requires a subscription.

item.title: Estadão e Record firmam parceria para debates presidenciais e ao governo de São Paulo
item.description: Estadão and Record have partnered to host presidential and São Paulo gubernatorial debates in the 2026 elections. The presidential debate is scheduled for September 27 (first round) and, if needed, October 18 (second round), both at 9 PM. The São Paulo gubernatorial debate will take place on September 21 at 1:25 PM, with a potential second round on October 13 at 1:20 PM. The partnership aims to expand access to high-quality debates amid an expected polarization between Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ).

item.title: O Rio em julgamento
item.description: The STF's judgment on whether the election to replace former Rio de Janeiro Governor Cláudio Castro — who resigned to avoid an almost certain impeachment — will be indirect or direct is triggering a realignment of forces within the Court, with potential consequences for upcoming cases like the Banco Master matter. Castro stepped down to evade a near-certain removal, and the outcome of this decision may affect the political and juridical balance in the tribunal.

item.title: Por que não é possível se candidatar sem partido no Brasil
item.description: Brazil's 1988 Constitution mandates party affiliation as a mandatory requirement for running for elective office, reinforcing pluripartisanship as the foundation of post-dictatorship democracy. This rule was upheld by the Supreme Court and the Elections Law (9.597/97), which prohibit independent candidacies, as parties are responsible for organizing candidacies, structuring campaigns, and ensuring governability. Experts state that Brazil's electoral system is structured around parties, making independent candidacies incompatible with the institutional design.

item.title: Fala de Lula sobre Moraes mostra que roteiro para se descolar do caso Master precisa de ajuste
item.description: Lula acknowledged that trying to hide or downplay the Master case is no longer viable, as the Supreme Court's image is tarnished and the scandal could spill over to his government. In an interview with ICL, he said the Court must provide a convincing explanation to society and that justices cannot become millionaires improperly. The president signaled that the strategy of silence needs to be revised amid growing public pressure.

item.title: Em mensagens, presidenciável do MBL relatava uso de cogumelos mágicos
item.description: Renan Santos, a presidential pre-candidate from the MBL, privately admitted in messages from the Cannipapo Instagram group to using magic mushrooms (Psilocybe cubensis), describing psychedelic experiences and confirming consumption. Despite publicly campaigning against drug trafficking, he acknowledged using the substance at least twice between November 2024 and October 2025, as verified by Metrópoles and confirmed by Santos himself.

item.title: Regra que pode 'unificar' eleições no Rio nunca foi aplicada pela Justiça Eleitoral para governadores
item.description: A 2018 TSE resolution allows supplementary elections to be held on the same date as ordinary ones in exceptional cases, but this rule has never been applied for governors. During the STF trial on Rio’s supplementary gubernatorial election, ministers suggested using this rule to unify elections in October, though experts note no precedent exists at the state level. Minister Fux voted for an indirect election, limited to state deputies of Alerj.

item.title: A eleição que pode acabar no primeiro turno
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian presidential election could be decided in the first round, as it was in 1998, the last time this occurred. Analysts consider this possibility real, despite the absence of 'sudden death' rules in electoral processes. The content is an exclusive article for subscribers, encouraging access through registration at the publication's link.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro amplia opções de vice no PP e eleva pressão sobre Tereza Cristina
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro has expanded his options for vice president in his pre-campaign, testing PP names to pressure Tereza Cristina into accepting the ticket. The vice-presidential pick hinges on a broader agreement between PP and União Brasil, which faces internal resistance due to the PL’s gains during the party window. If the federation fails, Minas Gerais Governor Romeu Zema emerges as a backup option for the bolsonarist ticket.

item.title: 'A Rede não tem dono' x 'retomar valores': entenda o embate entre Marina e a cúpula do partido, ligada a Heloísa Helena
item.description: The internal conflict in Rede Sustentability intensified between the national leadership, led by Paulo Lamac and allied with Heloísa Helena, and Marina Silva’s faction after she announced she would remain in the party to 'recover core values'. The party leadership claims democratic election and rejects accusations of authoritarianism, stating the party has no owner and must respect collective decisions. Marina, despite internal rifts and offers from the PT and PSB, reiterated her commitment to the party she helped found, keeping alive her potential Senate candidacy on Haddad’s ticket.

item.title: Lula teve encontro com Alcolumbre três dias antes de mandar mensagem de indicação de Messias ao Senado
item.description: Three days before sending the presidential message nominating Jorge Messias to the STF, Lula met with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre at the Alvorada Palace, accompanied by Rodrigo Pacheco. Although Alcolumbre did not guarantee approval, Lula felt the resistance to Messias had eased, with Pacheco also discussing his Minas gubernatorial bid with Lula’s backing.

item.title: De ex-ministros de Lula a auxiliares de Bolsonaro: os nomes na lista de pagamentos do Master, que soma R$ 66 milhões
item.description: The Master Bank reported to the Federal Revenue at least R$65.83 million in payments to party officials, former ministers, and a former president between 2023 and 2025, according to documents obtained by O GLOBO. The recipients include figures linked to both Lula’s government and Bolsonaro’s allies. Bank owner Daniel Vorcaro is detained on suspicion of fraud, while beneficiaries deny wrongdoing and claim legitimate relations with the institution.

item.title: Como fica o mapa dos governos estaduais com as trocas e renúncias para eleição 2026
item.description: Following the end of the incompatibility window, 10 states and the Federal District have new governors, reshaping the map of support for the 2026 presidential pre-candidates. Lula (PT) lost backing in Espírito Santo but retains support in 11 states, while Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) gained support in Acre and sees Amazonas and Rio de Janeiro under interim leadership. The PSD expanded its governorships to six, becoming the party with the strongest state presence.

item.title: MG decide de novo? Estado mais disputado segue indefinido para eleição
item.description: Minas Gerais, Brazil's second-largest electoral college, remains undecided for the 2026 elections, with Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro vying for support in a highly polarized scenario. In 2022, the state recorded the tightest result in the country, with Lula winning by just 50.2% to 49.8%, a margin of fewer than 50,000 votes. Despite efforts from both sides, neither has secured a solid electoral base in Minas, while the PL has yet to decide whether to run its own candidate or ally with figures like Cleitinho or Mateus Simões.

item.title: Brasil se encamina a unas elecciones sin mujeres candidatas a la presidencia por primera vez en más de 20 años
item.description: Brazil may hold its 2026 presidential election without any female candidates for the first time since 2002. The race is shaping up to be between Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, seeking re-election, and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving house arrest. Other pre-candidates, such as Ronaldo Caiado, are also men from right-wing parties, highlighting the lack of female representation in the presidential race.

item.title: La última barrabasada de ‘The Boys’: “Es importante reírse de la gente que da miedo”
item.description: The final season of 'The Boys' uses exaggerated violence and absurd humor to deliver a sharp political satire, mirroring the real-world chaos of the United States during Donald Trump’s presidency. Creator Eric Kripke admits reality has surpassed fiction, making satire harder as the world has become more absurd than the show itself. The first two episodes are now available on Amazon Prime Video, concluding a run that began in 2019 and will end in 2026.

item.title: STF volta a julgar ações sobre eleições no Rio nesta quinta; entenda em que ponto está o caso
item.description: The STF resumed judgment on the election for Rio de Janeiro governor following Claudio Castro's resignation. Minister Cristiano Zanin voted for a direct election, while Luiz Fux advocated an indirect choice via the state legislature. The justices also debated the validity of the state law regarding secret or open voting and the 24-hour disassociation period for candidates.

item.title: Primeiro dia de julgamento sobre eleições do Rio tem críticas ao TSE, alusão ao crime e à 'degradação política' do estado
item.description: On the first day of the STF's judgment on Rio de Janeiro's supplementary elections, ministers debated between direct and indirect voting, criticizing the TSE and emphasizing political degradation and organized crime's influence in the state. Cristiano Zanin defended popular vote, while Luiz Fux supports election by state deputies, citing the 'acephaly' of the Rio Executive. PSD lawyers compared Rio to Gotham City and pointed to politicians' arrests as symptoms of institutional contamination by crime.

item.title: Ala do STF que defende eleições diretas no Rio reforça argumento sobre ‘precedente’ e ‘fraude’ com renúncia de Castro
item.description: STF justices emphasized the 'precedent' argument and the alleged fraud in former governor Cláudio Castro's resignation to avoid TSE disqualification, advocating for direct elections for Rio de Janeiro's state government. Flávio Dino and Alexandre de Moraes questioned whether the fraud was properly examined in Castro's TSE trial, stressing that the resignation should be assessed as a potential maneuver to evade the consequences of conviction. The trial, tied at 1-1, will resume with Flávio Dino as the first voter this Thursday.

item.title: Polarização é prenúncio de situação antidemocrática, diz Moreira Franco
item.description: Former minister Wellington Moreira Franco warned that rising polarization, intolerance, and intransigence in Brazil signal a looming antidemocratic situation. He made the remarks during the launch of his book in Brasília, attended by Centrão figures and national political leaders. The book, based on over 100 hours of interviews, traces Brazil’s redemocratization journey.

item.title: Depoimento de Galípolo à CPI do Crime Organizado sobre caso Master irrita o Planalto
item.description: Central Bank President Gabriel Galípolo irritated the Planalto by testifying before the Organized Crime CPI and refusing to blame his predecessor, Roberto Campos Neto, for the Banco Master scandal, contrary to the Lula administration's expectations that he would assign fault to the Bolsonaro-appointee. Despite Lula's public accusations and political pressure, Galípolo stated that BC investigations found no evidence of Campos Neto's involvement in favor of Master, fueling government discontent, particularly over the BC's delay in cutting interest rates.

item.title: Justiça suspende imposto de 12% sobre exportação de petróleo
item.description: Federal Judge Humberto de Vasconcelos Sampaio suspended the 12% export tax on crude oil, instituted by Lula's government via provisional measure in March 2026, ruling that the measure's explicit goal of raising revenue violates constitutional principles and the anteriority requirement. The decision grants a security injunction filed by five oil and gas multinationals (Shell, Equinor, TotalEnergies, Repsol Sinopec, Petrogal), who argue the tax was misused as a fiscal tool rather than a regulatory one. The government had projected R$ 32.1 billion in revenue for 2026 to address urgent fiscal needs.

item.title: Câmara tem sete candidatos à vaga no TCU; Odair Cunha lidera apoios
item.description: Seven federal deputies have formally announced their candidacies for the Chamber’s vacancy at the TCU, with Odair Cunha (PT-MG) leading in declared support, backed by Chamber President Hugo Motta and 11 parties besides the PT. The hearings will take place on Monday, the 13th, in the Committee on Finance and Taxation, with approved nominees proceeding to a floor vote. Other named candidates include Soraya Santos (PL-RJ), Elmar Nascimento (União Brasil-BA), Hugo Leal (PSD-RJ), and Danilo Forte (PP-CE); two additional candidates are not explicitly named in the provided excerpt.

item.title: As candidaturas fictícias a deputado federal por São Paulo
item.description: The TSE upheld the PROS party's federal deputy candidate list in São Paulo for the 2022 elections, acknowledging the existence of fictitious female candidacies (laranjas) of Mariana Papaiz and Andréa Pradella, but ruled that their removal did not violate the legal 30% minimum gender participation requirement. Despite the gender quota fraud, the court rejected the total cancellation of the ticket, as the party still met the quota even without the fictitious candidates. Relator Kassio Nunes Marques and other ministers voted to disqualify the two women for eight years, while Estela Aranha issued a partial dissent, arguing that sanctions depend on actual breach of the quota.

item.title: Moraes determina que PM-DF declare perda de cargo de oficiais condenados por omissão no 8 de janeiro
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes ordered the DF Military Police to declare the loss of public offices for five former officials convicted of omission in the January 8 attacks, including former commander-general Fábio Augusto Vieira. The ruling confirms that loss of rank and patent applies even to officers in paid reserve, based on STF precedent.

item.title: Nikolas diz que candidaturas do PL em Minas vão servir à campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro à Presidência
item.description: Federal deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) stated that the PL’s candidacies in Minas Gerais will strengthen Senator Flávio Bolsonaro’s (PL-RJ) 2026 presidential campaign, stressing the need to unite the right to defeat the PT. He downplayed recent tensions with Eduardo Bolsonaro (PL-SP), emphasizing the shared goal of winning the election and highlighting the importance of reaching voters beyond the party’s base, citing the 50,000-vote margin that separated Bolsonaro from Lula in Minas Gerais in 2022 as proof that every vote matters.

item.title: “O PL/PR está gigante e os adversários desesperados”, diz Moro
item.description: Senator and Paraná gubernatorial pre-candidate Sérgio Moro posted a photo alongside Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) and federal deputy Filipe Barros (PL), claiming the party in Paraná is 'giant' and opponents 'desperate'. He reiterated his ambition to transform the state into a governance model, without specifying concrete policies.

item.title: Witzel pede voto secreto em eleição indireta no Rio
item.description: Wilson Witzel criticized the indirect election process for the governor of Rio de Janeiro, calling it illegitimate, referencing his own 2021 impeachment. He attended the STF hearing on the election format following Cláudio Castro’s resignation and sought to intervene in the discussion.

item.title: Câmara aprova em 1º turno PEC que garante recursos mínimos para assistência social
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved in first turn PEC 383/17, which mandates 1% of the net current revenue of the Union, states, Federal District, and municipalities to be allocated to the Unified Social Assistance System (Suas), with a phased implementation starting at 0.3% in the first year. The proposal received 464 favorable votes and 16 against, and still requires a second-round vote in the Chamber before proceeding to the Senate. Supporters emphasize that the fiscal impact is minimal compared to the social benefit, reaching 98 million Brazilians in vulnerable conditions.

item.title: Luisa Mell critica Janja por almoço de Páscoa com carne de paca
item.description: Luisa Mell criticized First Lady Janja for a video in which she prepares and serves paca meat to President Lula during an Easter lunch, calling the act 'unbelievably irresponsible'. The animal rights activist argued that consuming meat from wild animals is inappropriate and harmful to wildlife conservation. The video, circulating on social media, has sparked debate about dietary ethics and the use of natural resources by public figures.

item.title: Áudio: Cometer crimes diante de crianças e adolescentes pode virar agravante
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) had his bill PL 4.244/2025 approved by the Human Rights Commission, which proposes to increase penalties for crimes committed in the presence of minors, even if they are not direct victims. The initiative aims to strengthen criminal protection for children and adolescents. The bill will now be reviewed by the Constitution and Justice Commission (CCJ).

item.title: Ministros do STF debatem hipótese de manter governador interino do RJ até outubro e unificar eleições
item.description: STF justices are debating whether the succession for the Governor of Rio de Janeiro should occur via direct or indirect election. Relator Cristiano Zanin supports direct elections, while Luiz Fux advocates for an indirect choice via the state legislature. The possibility of unifying a supplementary election with the October regular election calendar was raised, which would keep interim governor Ricardo Couto in office until then, with the vote currently tied 1-1.

item.title: Lula aconselha Moraes a não participar de julgamentos do Banco Master
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva said he advised Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes not to participate in any potential rulings involving Banco Master, due to a financial contract between the bank and the law firm of Moraes’ wife, Viviane Barci. Lula made the recommendation during an interview with ICL, urging Moraes to declare himself disqualified to avoid a conflict of interest.

item.title: STF tem empate de 1×1 sobre formato das eleições no RJ; julgamento retorna quinta
item.description: The Supreme Court (STF) is tied 1×1 on whether the Rio de Janeiro governor’s succession should be decided by direct or indirect elections, following Cláudio Castro’s conviction for abuse of power. Minister Cristiano Zanin supported direct elections, arguing Castro’s resignation was an attempt to evade electoral justice, while Luiz Fux backed indirect elections, challenging the PSD’s legal standing to bring the case. The judgment will resume on Thursday, April 9.

item.title: TSE cassa mandato de prefeito por envolvimento com facção ligada ao Comando Vermelho
item.description: The TSE annulled the mandates of Mayor André Luís Almeida Coutinho (Avante) and Vice Mayor Camila Lucena (PP) of Cabedelo (PB) due to involvement in a vote-buying scheme, voter coercion, and misuse of public resources to benefit the Tropa do Amigão faction, linked to the Red Command. New elections are scheduled for April 12.

item.title: Petrobras ouviu indignação de Lula e acertou ao demitir diretor, diz Silveira
item.description: Mines and Energy Minister Alexandre Silveira stated that Petrobras made the right decision in dismissing Director of Logistics, Commercialization and Markets Claudio Schlosser, following public criticism from President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva regarding a cooking gas auction deemed inappropriate.

item.title: Cassado em votação aberta, Witzel acompanha julgamento no STF e defende sigilo em eventual eleição indireta no Rio
item.description: Former Governor Wilson Witzel, removed via open vote in the Rio State Assembly, attended the STF hearing on the electoral model for Rio's governorship following Claudio Castro's resignation. He argued that if an indirect election is held, deputies' votes must be secret, claiming Castro's resignation was a 'fraud' to avoid a direct election and keep his faction in power. Witzel also stated his 2020 impeachment process was illegitimate and politically pressured.

item.title: Entenda o 1º dia de julgamento no STF sobre a eleição para governador do Rio
item.description: The STF began judging actions regarding the Rio de Janeiro gubernatorial election after the resignation and ineligibility of Cláudio Castro. Cristiano Zanin voted for a direct election, arguing the resignation was a strategic move to avoid TSE disqualification and force an indirect vote controlled by Alerj, while Luiz Fux supported an indirect election per constitutional rules for vacancies in the last two years of the term. The PGR backed the claim of legal fraud, and the hearing continues Thursday, including debates on interim governance and the validity of state law on indirect elections.

item.title: Judiciário é visto como maior ameaça à democracia, diz pesquisa
item.description: A survey by Canal Meio and consultancy Ideia shows that 42.5% of respondents view the imbalance of powers — particularly judicial overreach — as the main threat to Brazil’s democracy, surpassing corruption, cited by only 16.5%. Polarization (13%), misinformation (9.7%), and foreign influence in elections (9.1%) are also significant concerns. President Lula warned that accusations against STF ministers and banker Daniel Vorcaro could be exploited by the opposition, especially in Senate races, potentially harming the government ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: “Sou avesso a empresas totalmente públicas”, diz Silveira
item.description: Minister of Mines and Energy Alexandre Silveira (PSD) stated he is opposed to fully public companies, advocating for mixed-capital models with Union participation as more efficient and strategic. He also commented on the removal of Claudio Romeo Schlosser from Petrobras' board following criticism of the LPG auction with above-reference prices, saying President Lula acted correctly. Silveira said the government is working to prevent direct pass-through of international fuel price increases to Brazilian consumers.
